items.title: Global Macro Strategy: Midterms Reaction
items.summary: While geopolitical and AI-financing risks will likely persist, we think investors have de-risked sufficiently and equities can rise. We prefer to express this view in European equities, which benefit more from oil prices' fall and are less exposed to a slowdown in the data-center buildout.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: The Day After the Midterms
items.summary: Markets had their usual response to a blue wave: yields lower, USD lower, equities up. We'd be wary of seeing signal from these moves, as they could just be the typical historical response given expectations for less spending and the vol crush effect. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: UK Raises Rates, But We See Nuance in Its Decision
items.summary: The UK raised rates 25 basis points, with a unanimous vote interpreted as making a December hike more likely. But we see the decision as more nuanced, and policymakers were clear that decisions will be meeting by meeting, shaped by energy prices and the outcome of wage settlements.

items.title: Oil Monitor: Potential Impacts of the Midterms' Blue Wave
items.summary: The blue wave has added to momentum for a U.S.-Iran deal, leading oil and global gas markets to sell off, though the potential for renewed escalation remains. Brent oil prices fell to $95 a barrel, and TTF to 85 EUR/MWh at the time of this writing. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Themes to Watch at Our 2026 China Conference
items.summary: Our flagship China Conference will be held Nov. 10-13 in Shanghai and Shenzhen. Our equity teams, economists and strategists highlight key themes to watch at this year’s conference, with our guide covering macroeconomic trends, policy direction, sector outlooks and investment ideas.

items.title: Middle East Oil & Gas: Headline Risks and Potential Playbooks
items.summary: Eight months into the Gulf crisis, we note that MENA Energy hasn't seen a widespread de-rating despite significant challenges to asset integrity; and that where de-rating has occurred, it may offer downside protection in the event of a resolution as well as potential earnings leverage.

items.title: U.S. Oil Services and Exploration & Production: Midterms Reaction
items.summary: The midterms drove disparate responses across the Energy complex. We offer some perspective on the moves, starting with the observation that amid heightened crude volatility, it's important to focus on key secular themes including deepwater oil, international shale and international gas.

items.title: We're Initiating Coverage of ATI at Buy
items.summary: We initiate coverage of ATI with a Buy rating and a $229 target price, representing 28% upside. We think ATI's increasing OEM production and multiyear margin transformation are likely to fuel revenue and earnings growth above consensus in 2027 and beyond, and offer further analysis herein.

items.title: We're Upgrading Coupang to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading Coupang to Buy, given likely sequential improvement in adjusted EBITDA; its developing offering business likely being less of earnings headwind in 2027; and analysis that suggests CPNG's share price is now near floor value. We offer further thoughts in this note.

items.title: Brazil Pharmaceuticals: Here Wegovy Again!
items.summary: At first glance, ANVISA’s approval of oral Wegovy in Brazil is clearly positive for GLP-1 adoption, potentially unlocking a pool of needle-averse patients while supporting treatment continuity. But as noted herein, we'd caution against fully extrapolating U.S. and UK trends to Brazil.

items.title: Japan FX: Is a USDJPY Downtrend Ahead?
items.summary: With the midterms behind us, we expect a clear downtrend in the USDJPY to emerge over the long term, but note the risk of JPY weakness will continue to smolder in the short to medium term. In the near term, keys will be U.S. equities' performance and the impacts of the U.S.-Iran conflict.

items.title: Off the Cuff: Assessing Markets' Response to the Midterms
items.summary: With the midterms behind us, we look at how embedded sentiment has been about three aspects of President Trump's policies: tariffs, Iran and spending. We explore how far sentiment-driven repositioning can run and consider the push and pull between sentiment and fundamentals.

items.title: We're Downgrading Adobe to Sell
items.summary: We're downgrading Adobe to Sell, seeing downside risk to consensus growth estimates into FY27. New CEO Anil Chakravarty takes over in December and we expect strategic changes to Adobe’s Creative business, potentially at the expense of near-term growth. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: AMD Sees AI Sales Reaching Escape Velocity
items.summary: We maintain AMD as our top Buy-rated large-cap growth compute semis pick following its "beat and raise" results. Management now sees data-center AI as the largest business within AMD; with the AI business reaching escape velocity, investor focus shifts to executing a multiyear ramp.

items.title: Arista Networks' First Look at 2027 Is Better Than Expected
items.summary: Arista's results topped expectations as strong AI and Enterprise customer demand delivered record topline growth, and delivered above-consensus FY27 guidance. ANET expects long-term growth above the market’s ~24% five-year CAGR, due to share gains. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: We're Upgrading Ferrovial to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading Ferrovial to Buy. We think the market is discounting both the group's growth trajectory, underpinned by its high-quality concession assets, as well as the recent U.S. P3 project wins. We estimate ~13% EPS CAGR over 2027-30 and see an attractive entry point for investors.

items.title: U.S. Electric Utilities: What's Texas's Data-Center Outlook Now?
items.summary: Greg Abbott was voted out as Texas governor, with data centers a top campaign issue. We think the new administration has a mandate to put in strong public protections around new data centers. which will likely slow approvals and become a key focus in the state's 2027 legislative session.

items.title: Global Quantitative Macro Strategy: The Great Tech Selloff
items.summary: Our flow model has completed a decisive rotation out of Technology, establishing Materials, Communications, and Health Care as the preferred longs. We see market conditions as having moved firmly away from Goldilocks and toward the late-cycle Tightening Financial Conditions.

items.title: Latin America's Reform Agenda: From Mandate to Delivery
items.summary: Latin America's reform window is now being tested, as six new governments plus Brazil look to convert electoral mandates into legislative outcomes. We look at the legislative arithmetic for reform and explore how the next six weeks will compress the execution test into the budget cycle.

items.title: Coffee Fundamentals Remain Loose as Demand Begins to Crack
items.summary: Coffee prices have been volatile and changed direction repeatedly over the last six months, while Brazilian exports have remained exceptionally strong. We evaluate regional supply dynamics in the context of a strengthening El Niño and also examine coffee demand through an equities lens.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: Midterms, Geopolitics and Staying Bearish AUD
items.summary: The combination of U.S. midterms and the Treasury refunding announcement should see lower yields and lower USD. But we think geopolitical risks will likely stay elevated given Middle East tensions. Separately, we remain short AUDUSD after the RBA’s “dovish hike.”

items.title: MENA Emerging Markets: Key North Africa Themes Into 2027
items.summary: We look at key macroeconomic themes with the potential to shape 2027 across North Africa, from tentative signs of growth and the inflation picture to the challenges of high debt levels and our thoughts on exchange rates.

items.title: U.S. Banks Face New Era of Balance-Sheet Management
items.summary: The Financial Accounting Standards Board is finalizing an Accounting Standards Update that will permit banks to apply fair value/cash flow hedge accounting to their extensive Held-to-Maturity securities portfolios. We delve into the proposed details and key implications for the sector.

items.title: India Economics: Labor Markets and AI Disruption
items.summary: We look at India's labor market and its exposure to AI, which yields a range of scenarios. A potential challenge: High AI exposure sectors have a disproportionately large share of total corporate wage cost (~42%), especially among the unlisted companies. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Apple Posts Better-Than-Expected Results But Offers Mixed Outlook
items.summary: Apple reported better-than-expected results but a mixed outlook, with higher product revenues seen as partially offset by lower services growth and gross margins. Despite the mixed outlook, we remain constructive on Buy-rated AAPL's long-term trajectory and see it as a defensive stock.

items.title: Sovereign AI Strength Drives Revenue Acceleration at Palantir
items.summary: Palantir delivered another top-line blowout in the third quarter, with especially strong fourth-quarter guidance, helped by surging demand for PLTR's Sovereign AI motion. We raise our estimates considerably, upping our ’26-’27 revenue, EPS and FCF forecasts 4% to 7%.

items.title: Is a Bow Wave Building for Behind-the-Meter Contracts?
items.summary: A key takeaway from our August Energy Conference was bullishness from behind-the-meter power players about a slew of new projects. This bow wave may have been kicked off by an announcement from SEI, with other players possibly nearing announcements of their own, as explored in this note.

items.title: China Banks Saw a Strong Quarter on Trading Gains
items.summary: China banks posted stronger-than-expected pre-provision operating profit growth of 13.8% year over year in the third quarter on strong trading gains, resilient loan growth and stable net interest margin. Earnings growth was slower, but we still see it as representing decent acceleration.

items.title: Australia Raises Rates to an 18-Year High
items.summary: Australia raised rates 25 basis points, marking its fifth hike in seven meetings, with policymakers noting persistent inflation and a growing risk of unanchored inflation expectations. Our base case is for no hike in December, but with risks clearly skewed toward higher rates into 2027.

items.title: What's Ahead for Growth in Saudi Arabia?
items.summary: Saudi Arabia's real GDP expanded 1.3% quarter on quarter in seasonally adjusted terms, ending two straight declining quarters. We look at how alternative fourth-quarter crude-oil production paths could shape the full-year outcome, and how that forecast compares with official projections.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Model: Flow Rotation Persists
items.summary: Positioning trends continue to diverge across regions. U.S. large-cap positioning has moderated further as increased short flows pushed the S&P 500 and Nasdaq positioning closer to neutral, reducing downside liquidation risk but underscoring cautious investor sentiment.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Revenue Growth Accelerates
items.summary: We continue to see the market as underestimating AI-driven revenue growth at the hyperscalers despite upward revisions and ongoing infrastructure constraints. We expect accelerating enterprise adoption to sustain the AI trade, despite bottlenecks around equipment, regulation and financing.

items.title: We're Downgrading Volvo to Neutral
items.summary: We're downgrading Volvo to Neutral and lowering our target price to SEK318. Our Buy rating rested on likely margin upside in Trucks into 2027 on improved price/cost and improving mix, but we no longer see this playing out. We offer further analysis of what may lie ahead in this note.

items.title: We're Downgrading Arthur J. Gallagher to Neutral
items.summary: We're downgrading Arthur J. Gallagher to Neutral. The stock appears to reasonably discount the outlook, and we lack a differentiated view on the company’s prospects. We note that AJG is trading at a ~10% premium to peers (on P/E and EV/EBITDA) vs. near parity historically.

items.title: China Re-Anchors Its Primary Policy Rate
items.summary: China formally shifted its primary policy rate from 7D to O/N reverse repo rate, a major step in central-banking reform. We look at three key issues still to be addressed. We see this as a mark-to-market adjustment rather than a de facto rate cut, and don't expect a November LPR cut.

items.title: European Aerospace & Defense: As the Earnings Dust Settles...
items.summary: After a volatile week, we apply a reverse-DCF framework to assess what long-term profit growth is required to justify current Aerospace share prices. For openers, Airbus is pricing in just 2% long-term growth, which we view as too conservative given 3-4% traffic growth plus pricing.

items.title: MENA Investors Gird for Conflict Escalation
items.summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict has had a varied impact on MENA regional equities: Sectors such as energy and consumer staples have remained relatively resilient, with real estate and banks pressured. Given potential for escalation, we highlight preferred sector positioning and key vulnerabilities.

items.title: Africa Economics & Strategy Weekly: Kenyan Politics Re-Align
items.summary: We look at the evolving political background in Kenya in the run-up to next year’s elections and explore what's behind this year's broad stability for the Kenyan shilling, despite a rise in global oil prices having driven a deterioration in current account dynamics.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: The Disappearing Hawks Trick
items.summary: Rates continue to benefit from the flight to quality though it remains fickle at times. We roll forward our received October FOMC trade into a December/January FOMC flattener to monetize a likely skip in January. Separately, we see reduced hawkish tail risks as supportive for carry trades.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: Haunted by Rate Hikes
items.summary: Investors are appropriately pricing in downside scenarios related to a slowdown in AI-related spending despite strong economic growth. Our base case is for another 25-basis-point hike in December, but we wouldn't be surprised if the Fed's next move is a cut.

items.title: Emerging Markets Economic Outlook & Strategy: The Widening Wedge
items.summary: The U.S.-led AI capex boom appears to be widening growth differentiation across emerging markets, while most non-AI EMs face tighter funding conditions without a commensurate boost. Moreover, we see China’s policies further adding pressure to traditional manufacturing sectors.

items.title: Global Asset Allocation: Risk Appetite Under Pressure
items.summary: We recently cut our equity risk in reaction to our POLLS index. This is a purely tactical indicator, but we take it seriously given risks of a US.-Iran escalation and continued AI financing fears. But our inclination is to buy the dip when the Iran endgame becomes clearer or AI fears fade.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: More Trick Than Treat
items.summary: This week’s price action conjures recollections of Tech bubble trading when markets had a way of defending views toward related securities even as fundamental cracks in the bull narrative began to unfold. This week’s mega-cap earnings are the current case in point, as we explore herein.

items.title: Alphabet Sees AI Mode Create Search Monetization Headwinds
items.summary: Alphabet results came in slightly below consensus expectations. We look at three investor debates that are likely to emerge from the quarter. We lower our target price to $375 from $447 and acknowledge near-term headwinds, but remain constructive on Buy-rated GOOGL.

items.title: AWS Growth Outlook Reinforces Amazon's Expanding AI Opportunity
items.summary: We emerge from Amazon's results incrementally positive on shares though AWS revenue growth of 39.3% year over year came in below elevated investor expectations. Looking at AMZN's growth AWS outlook, we note a relatively clear path to $1 trillion in revenue over the next five to 10 years.

items.title: Intel: Two Steps Forward, One Step Back
items.summary: Intel reported a strong beat but provided a weak outlook due to a host of factors. We remain believers in Intel's technology and its foundry vision, but expect the debate on the stock to shift, reflecting issues that we explore in this note.

items.title: Eli Lilly Shows Momentum With Multiple Forward Paths
items.summary: We think Lilly's underlying business is starting to receive the attention it deserves and continue to see robust growth that remains unparalleled among its peers, with drivers that reinforce Buy-rated LLY's position as our favorite large Biopharma. We raise our target price to $1,650.

items.title: Metal Matters: Lithium Prices to Stay Depressed in the Near Term
items.summary: Spot lithium prices have fallen 40% since September, raising the question of whether the correction has run its course. Given the backdrop, explored herein, we see little catalyst for a meaningful recovery in downstream activity at current prices. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: OATs Enter the Reaction Function
items.summary: While the ECB was dominated by President Lagarde’s early departure, it offered an important signal that OATs have entered the reaction function, although spread widening is not yet sufficient to derail a December rate hike. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Global Economic Outlook & Strategy: A Tenuous Balance
items.summary: The global economy is still powering ahead even as uncertainties — from the sustainability of the AI boom to geopolitics — continue to mount. We see global growth coming in at 2.7% this year and climbing to 2.8% next year, as pressures from the U.S.-Iran conflict eventually moderate.
